assumptions: Both arms and both legs work symmetrically, so the exercise is bilateral and every action uses working sides.
Hip, knee and ankle extension drive the load. The ankle is marked assist because it contributes little to moving the load.
The arms stay straight during the pull and bend only to guide the dumbbells to the shoulders, so elbow flexion is marked assist.
No scapular elevation (shrug) is listed because the instructions do not cue it.
The spine stays neutral under load, so the back works through anti_flexion_spine rather than lumbar movement.
The dumbbells are held in the hands throughout, so grip is required. Heavy bracing applies to the explosive pull and catch.
classification_reasons: Bilateral standing dumbbell clean from the floor: hip hinge/squat setup, triple extension, then a catch at the shoulders.
The olympic_lift family and the hip, knee, ankle and elbow action vocabulary represent it faithfully.

The contact sheet matches the text: the start frame shows a hip-hinged, knees-bent pull position with a dumbbell in each hand at the floor, and the later frame shows an upright stance with the dumbbells at shoulder height.

instructions: Begin standing with a dumbbell in each hand with your feet shoulder width apart.
Lower the weights to the floor by flexing at the hips and knees, pushing your hips back until the dumbbells reach the floor. This will be your starting position.

To initiate the movement, violently jump upward by extending the hips, knees, and ankles to acclerate the weights upward. Maintaining a neutral grip on the dumbbells, keep the arms straight until full extension is reached.
After full extension, rebend the hips and knees to receive the weight in a squat position. Allow the arms to bend, guiding the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Upon receiving the weight in the squat position, extend the hips and knees to finish in a standing position with the weights on your shoulders.
